inputBoundary: One caller-supplied finite daily self-perceived stress score within the source-disclosed closed anchor range 1 through 7. Survey response parsing, score serialization, participant identity, and day attribution occur upstream.
outputBoundary: Emit source label 0 (not stressed) when score is below or equal to 4, including the neutral anchor 4, and source label 1 (stressed) when score is above 4.
limitations: The publication says a 'seven items scale' and provides anchors 1, 4, and 7, but does not provide item text or establish whether this means seven items or seven response points; this binding therefore accepts an already-derived numeric score and does not infer questionnaire construction.
The source does not disclose raw response serialization or an integer-only storage type, so this binding validates the closed source anchor range without imposing integer-only input.
A missing, nonfinite, below-anchor, or above-anchor score fails closed before classification.
Participant identity joins, evening-survey delivery, day attribution, missing-response handling, and the consecutive-data cohort gate are outside this outcome-label boundary.

Feature engineering, normalization, participant-disjoint train/test splitting, leave-one-subject-out evaluation, model fitting, and reported cohort percentages are downstream and are not reproduced by this binding.
The captured arXiv archive is publication source, not released target-analysis code or data, so this fixture proves the disclosed label transformation but not the paper's complete model outputs.
